newsitem.title: USA: Lawsuit fails to halt bond-financed Fla. bridge.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit fails to halt bond-financed Fla. bridge.

text.p: A federal judge in Florida has refused environmentalists' request to halt contruction on a bridge financed with $95 million of revenue bonds, the Santa Rosa Bay Bridge Authority chairman said Wednesday.
"The district judge has ruled in our favor," authority Chairman Mahan McCall said.

The Florida Wildlife Federation filed suit in August against the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which issued the permit for the 3.5 mile bridge connecting barrier islands in Santa Rosa Bay with the northwest Florida Panhandle.
The wildlife group said the bridge project would endanger environmentally sensitive wetlands.
A federal judge in Jacksonville dismissed the lawsuit with prejudice on Tuesday, meaning it cannot be modified or resubmitted.
The lawsuit briefly delayed the bond sale which had been set for August. The issue went forward via PaineWebber Inc in late October after the bridge authority arranged special insurance coverage.
"We came up with a unique environmental insurance coverage that would take effect in the event an injunction halted the bridge. That gave comfort to the bond holders," McCall said.
He said the coverage was provided by a consortium of insurance firms.
